shortName: Renaissance School of Medicine at Stony Brook University

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Renaissance School of Medicine is committed to admitting a diverse class each year. There are a number of student clubs and organizations which enhance the diversity cultural experience at Stony Brook: Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association (APAMSA), Latin Medical Student Association (LMSA), Student National Medical Association (SNMA), LGBTQ: OUTpatient, Jewish Student Union, Catholic Medical Association (CMA) and the Christian Medicine and Dental Association.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be granted to enable a student to resolve personal, health, or academic problems or to further her/his education away from the School of Medicine. Except for leaves granted pursuant to degree granting or other approved programs, the maximum cumulative leave of absence for personal or health problems or for supplemental education may not exceed a total of eighteen (18) months. All leaves of absence must be requested in writing and approved by the Vice Dean for UGME. The Vice Dean for UGME may specify conditions that must be met for the student to be permitted to return after the leave of absence.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Renaissance School of Medicine currently has over 60 student clubs and organizations.  These include clinical specialty interest groups, student government, cultural organizations, social activities, health and wellness activities and community service organizations.  Stony Brook is consistently cited for its high level of student involvement in extra-curricular activities and community service.  Most notably, Stony Brook HOME is a student run clinic which provides free medical services to the underserved population in a Long Island community.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Stony Brook University and the Renaissance School of Medicine are located 60 miles east of Manhattan on the north shore of Long Island. The campus is surrounded by a picturesque and historic community. The campus provides a wide spectrum of activities ranging from NCAA Division I sporting events to professional theater and fine arts. Students can participate in a wide range of intramural athletic activities.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: There is limited  graduate housing on campus.   Local off campus house/apartment sharing is the most popular housing option for RSOM students. Housing costs range from $800-$1000 per month (including utilities), with an average of  $900 per month.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The Renaissance SOM has support systems in place for gender and sexual minority students. 
1) There is an active student-run club for the LGBTQ+ community.
2) The Associate Dean for Minority Student Affairs meets with students from the LGBTQ+ community frequently to address their areas of concern.
3) All University students have access to the LGBTQ+ Center which seeks to create an open and inclusive environment for LGBTQ+ people in the Stony Brook community: https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/studentaffairs/lgbtq/center/lgbtqcenter.php
4)Stony Brook Medicine and Stony Brook Southampton have been designated as “Leaders in LGBTQ Healthcare Equality”  by the Human Rights Campaign for 2022-2024: https://www.stonybrookmedicine.edu/LGBTQ/goal
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The University Office of Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS) provides free and confidential services to all enrolled students at the university, including medical students.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Stony Brook University is New York’s flagship university and No. 1 public university. The Stony Brook campus lies about 60 miles east of Manhattan and 60 miles west of Montauk Point. It is only a short distance to the Atlantic beaches of the south shore and the vineyards of the East End. Our University aims to provide comprehensive undergraduate, graduate, and professional education of the highest quality; carry out research and intellectual endeavors of the highest international standards that advance knowledge and have immediate or long-range practical significance; provide leadership for economic growth, technology, and culture for neighboring communities and the wider geographic region; provide state-of-the-art innovative health care, while serving as a resource to a regional healthcare network and to the traditionally underserved; and fulfill these objectives while celebrating diversity and positioning the University in the global community.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Although not required, access to a vehicle is highly recommended. Public transportation to off-site clinical rotations and shopping are not readily available.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to wear their white coat and dress in a professional manner whenever they are interacting with actual or standardized patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Deans, faculty advisors, and course directors hold open hours each week. Academic support services, including tutoring and mentoring programs, are provided by two success coaches/learning specialists.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students interview standardized patients the first week of school and begin to learn the H & P in ICM. After 4 months they begin to care for patients in ambulatory, inpatient, and emergency settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Courses employ multiple pedagogies, with at least 50% of a course being delivered via active learning formats, team-based learning, small-group case discussions, OSCEs, simulations, labs, CPCs.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations are four 12-week blocks: Medicine (Internal Med & Primary Care); Mother-Child (Ob/Gyn & Peds); Acute Care (Surgery, Anesthes. & Emerg. Med); & Mind-Brain (Psych, Neuro & Radiology)
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures per se are not mandatory. However, class sessions that employ small-group, active learning strategies, such as TBL, PBL, CPC, case discussions, laboratories, etc., are mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Renaissance School of Medicine offers two curriculum tracks, the four-year LEARN and three-year 3YMD. Both tracks consist of 3 phases. The 18-month Phase I includes a sequence of four basic science courses – The Body, Molecular Foundations of Medicine, Pathogens and Host Defense, Basic Mechanisms of Disease, five integrated pathophysiology systems-based courses – Cardio/Pulmonary/Renal, Mind/Brain/Behavior, Endocrine/Reproductive, Gastrointestinal/Nutrition, Musculoskeletal, and three longitudinal courses – Introduction to Clinical Medicine, Themes in Medical Education, Medicine in Contemporary Society. Phase II consists of four 12-week clerkship blocks: Medicine-Primary Care, Ob/Gyn-Peds, Surgery-EM-Anesthesia, and Psych-Neurology-Radiology. A Well-being Week caps each block. Students in both the LEARN and 3YMD tracks complete Phases I & II together. In Phase III, LEARN students complete a selective, sub-internship, Advanced Clinical Experience, and 26 weeks of electives. 3YMD students complete a sub-internship and 6 weeks of electives. 3YMD students also complete 14 weeks of credit during the first and second summers. Transition courses are offered at significant training junctures – Transition to Medical School, Transition to Clinical Care, Transition to Residency.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Students complete a four-week Primary Care Clerkship that emphasizes prevention, diagnosis, and management of common primary care health issues in adults. Students may rotate with a Family Practitioner, General Internist, or Geriatrician, participating in all aspects of their preceptor’s clinical practice, including office visits, hospital rounds, nursing home visits, and home visits. Students receive individualized feedback from their preceptor, thus improving their communication, history and physical exam skills, and management skills, while gaining a realistic view of outpatient primary care practice. This clerkship also includes an interprofessional component in which students learn about hospice, home care, and transitions of care through a series of home visits supervised by nurses. In Phase III, students may take a two- or four-week elective in Primary Care, which also pairs them one-on-one with an experienced preceptor in a Primary Care office.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students can participate in research through the NIH-funded Medical Scientist Training Program (MD/PhD), the department-funded Scholarly Concentrations Program, and the Global Health-funded International Health Research Program. Students can also engage in clinical research projects with individual faculty members or departments.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Three phases: 18 month preclinical Phase I, 12 month primary clinical Phase II, 16 month advanced clinical Phase III
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students are able to participate in a host of community service and service learning opportunities, including a student-run free clinic, Stony Brook HOME.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students may complete a scholarly concentration in basic, clinical or translational research, global health, medical education, or medical humanities.  MD/PhD (MSTP), MD/MA, MD/MPH,MD/MSECR.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Stony Brook University Hospital and SBU Children's, SBU Southampton,  SBU Eastern Long Island Hospitals, Nassau Univ. Med. Center, Northport Veterans Affairs Med. Center, Mt. Sinai South Nassau Hosp.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Courses in Phase I are P/F. Phase II core clerkships (≥4 weeks) are H/HP/P/LP/F and mini-clerkships (2 weeks) are P/F. Clinical courses in Phase III are H/HP/P/LP/ and non-clinical electives are P/F.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The Renaissance School of Medicine at Stony Brook University is a public medical school in Stony Brook, New York. It is part of Stony Brook University, a flagship of the State University of New York (SUNY) system and one of 71 members of the Association of American Universities (AAU), the invitation-only organization of the best research universities in North America.

Renaissance School of Medicine is part of Stony Brook Medicine, the University’s medical enterprise, which encompasses Stony Brook University Hospital, Stony Brook Children’s Hospital, Stony Brook Southampton Hospital and the Long Island State Veterans Home, plus more than 100 outpatient care sites throughout Suffolk County. It is one of five schools of the Health Sciences at Stony Brook University, which also include Dental Medicine, Health Professions, Nursing and Social Welfare.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We are committed to recruiting and training diverse students, clinicians and physician-scientists in biomedical sciences to improve the health of all individuals and populations through education, outreach, compassionate care and research that discovers the biology of disease and informs novel preventive, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: Stony Brook University offers an integrated eight-year program for students interested in attending medical school following their undergraduate degree. The Scholars for Medicine (SFM) track offers selected students in the Honors College, WISE Program or University Scholars Program an opportunity to complete a combined Bachelor’s/MD course of study while participating in pre-medical classes and activities. Students accepted into any of these tracks are reserved a seat in the Renaissance School of Medicine upon graduation provided they complete all applicable program requirements. Successful applicants to the program (the middle 50th percentile ranges) have historically had 98-99 high school GPAs and 1490-1590 SAT composite scores. ACT exam scores are now considered in lieu SAT scores. The ACT range is 35-36. Candidates must also have documentation of U.S. citizenship or permanent residency in the United States.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: The Committee on Admissions requires a minimum of 2 letters of recommendation; one must be from a science professor.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants invited to interview will have 2 separate virtual interviews with a member of the Committee on Admissions. The Office of Admissions hosts virtual informational sessions for interviewed applicants on Wednesdays and Thursdays. The program includes a Medical Student Session and sessions with the Assistant Deans of Admissions, Diversity and Student Affairs and Financial Aid.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews are conducted via a virtual platform.
medSchoolApplication.secApplName: All verified applicants will receive an email for the secondary application
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Currently, students can apply for state residency after they have completed their first year of medical school. Determination of state residency is rendered by the Office of Student Accounts.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Applications are accepted from Out-of-state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Applications are accepted from Canadian applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Applications are accepted from International applicants.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Applications are accepted from DACA applicants.
medSchoolApplication.transferContact: Office of Admissions, Renaissance School of Medicine
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Please visit our website for  information about our admission policies and procedures: https://renaissance.stonybrookmedicine.edu/admissions
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The admissions process for the Renaissance School of Medicine is a holistic one and MCAT scores are reviewed as part of the holistic process. Please note, the oldest MCAT® considered is January 12, 2024.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We do not have a minimum GPA requirement. Our Committee on Admissions reviews all applications in a holistic manner.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We do not have a minimum of credit hours required. Our Committee on Admissions reviews all applications in a holistic manner.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We do accept coursework from community colleges, however, our expectations are that students complete the majority of their undergraduate coursework at a 4 year college or university.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of Intent, Letter of Interest and/or significant updates or achievements should be uploaded in our AMP Portal. Please email office if there are any questions: somadmissions@stonybrookmedicine.edu

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Stony Brook participates in the Federal Direct Unsubsidized Stafford and Federal Direct Grad PLUS loans.  Institutional need based grants and institutional scholarships are also available.  All financial aid applicants must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid and the RSOM Institutional Application for Financial Aid annually. Financial aid information and debt management counseling are available through the Office of Student Affairs. On-campus graduate student housing is available; off-campus housing is the most popular housing option for medical students.  Students are advised to have their own means of transportation  available because there is limited public transportation in the Stony Brook area and no public transportation to travel to outlying clinical facilities.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Renaissance School of Medicine in conjunction with the Associated Medical Schools of New York (AMSNY) offers a Postbaccalaureate graduate program with the Department of Physiology and Biophysics at Stony Brook University. This is a 30-credit Master of Science degree program, with a curricular emphasis on physiology and biomedical sciences. Students referred to the AMSNY Program through the Office of Admissions at the Renaissance School of Medicine, are guaranteed an acceptance to the Renaissance School of Medicine provided they maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better within the program, meet M.S. program curricular requirements, and earn an MCAT total score of ≥504 (with no less than 124 in any section; scores may not be interchanged from other exams). Eligible students may enroll in the 12-month or 18-month thesis degree program option.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: The Renaissance School of Medicine at Stony Brook University is on a rolling admissions basis.  Accepted applicants will be notified beginning October 15, 2024.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: We require all applicants to take CASPer. An application will be considered incomplete without this test result.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: 3YMD is a program that offers a limited number of students who have already been accepted into Renaissance School of Medicine at Stony Brook University's four-year MD program the opportunity to complete their MD in three years. Students who are accepted into the 3YMD then enter a directed pathway with the Stony Brook University Hospital specialty residency program of their choice.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Our process is on a rolling admissions cycle.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Our Committee on Admissions recommends a total of 15 credit hours for Chemistry. There is a minimum of 4 semesters recommended including coursework in general and organic chemistry and a course in biochemistry. A minimum of 3 semesters of lab is recommended. 2 semesters of Biology with lab are recommended. Please see table below for other recommended coursework.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Committee on Admissions will do a holistic review of your candidacy for medical school. Your ability, to some measure, will be evident in your academic record, your scores on competitive examinations, your faculty's statements and your extracurricular and work experiences. Candidates should be aware that the majority of those who apply to the Renaissance School of Medicine present exceptional credentials and the entering class reflects this fact. Motivational and personal characteristics as indicated in your application, letters of evaluation, and personal interviews are also a major part of our admissions assessment. The contribution you might make to our student body and the medical profession will, we hope, become apparent in reading your person statements and the comments of others.
